label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.74), PHQ-9 depression score (1.75), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.17) all sit in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring emotional distress. With 165 respondents in this cluster, it is a substantial group characterized by the convergence of heavy digital engagement and pronounced psychological burden.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen/internet use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily digital engagement (more than 5 hours)
Elevated loneliness despite high connectivity (UCLA-8 mean 1.74)
Highest anxiety levels among profiles (GAD-7 mean 2.17)
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety symptoms
tone: Concerned and empathetic; clinically attentive to the interplay between prolonged screen time and emotional well-being

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness, PHQ-9 depression, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below typical thresholds, these individuals appear to be psychologically well-adjusted and emotionally stable. They spend a moderate amount of time (1–3 hours) on activities captured in the study, suggesting balanced engagement rather than excessive or minimal use.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with 1–3 hours of daily usage
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77), indicating strong social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33), well below clinical concern
Near-floor anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.09), suggesting emotional calm and stability
Moderate daily usage of 1–3 hours, reflecting balanced and non-excessive engagement
Highly educated background, potentially associated with greater coping resources

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they do not exhibit the affective distress typically associated with loneliness, suggesting a degree of emotional resilience or effective coping that buffers against mood and anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level or higher education, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen/social-media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate-to-high perceived social isolation
Low depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) suggesting subclinical depression levels
Low anxiety symptom burden (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) indicating subclinical anxiety levels
Moderate and controlled digital engagement (1–3 hours daily)
Possible reliance on academic or professional pursuits as a coping mechanism given high educational attainment
tone: Quietly disconnected yet psychologically stable; introspective and self-sufficient rather than distressed
